watering_every_days.note: Pudina spreads via shallow runners (stolons) that dry out very quickly in intense Indian summer heat. Keep the soil evenly moist like a wrung-out sponge, but never stagnant. In hot May weather, water every morning; if leaves flag by late afternoon, give a gentle sip. In monsoon, ensure wide container drainage so rainwater never stagnates around roots.

soil.in_simple_words: Rich, moisture-retentive, organically rich loamy soil in a wide, shallow pot or trough that allows creeping runners to root freely.
soil.mix_recipe: 2 parts garden loam + 2 parts vermicompost or well-decomposed cow dung manure (gobar khaad) + 1 part coco peat + 1 part coarse river sand + 2 tbsp neem cake powder

pet_and_child_safety.note: Completely non-toxic to humans and safe for culinary use in chutneys and drinks. Safe around dogs and cats in normal fresh garden nibbles, though large ingestions of fresh mint leaves or concentrated mint essential oils should be avoided as menthol can cause mild tummy upset in pets.

common_problems.problem: Midday heat wilting and scorched crispy leaf edges
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are mint leaves drooping limp by midday and developing crisp brown margins under harsh 38°C+ summer sun?
solve_it_like_this: Move the pot to a bright balcony position that receives gentle morning sun and shade during blazing afternoon hours.
Apply a 1-inch top layer of organic mulch (coco peat or dried sugarcane bagasse) to insulate shallow roots from rapid evaporation.
Water thoroughly every morning until water drains out from the bottom; avoid tiny shallow surface sprinkles.

common_problems.problem: Aphids and two-spotted spider mites on tender sprigs
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Do you see clusters of tiny soft green or black bugs on fresh shoot tips, or pale dusty speckling with fine webs underneath leaves?
solve_it_like_this: Never spray chemical or systemic insecticides on edible herbs. Blast the foliage vigorously with a sharp morning jet of clean water to dislodge pests.
Spray an organic emulsion of 5 ml cold-pressed neem oil and 2 ml gentle liquid soap per litre of water thoroughly under all leaves in late evening.
Regularly harvest top sprigs; pruning stimulates vigorous clean new runners and removes pest harboring tips.

common_problems.problem: Rootbound runner congestion and bare woody stems
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are center stems turning woody and leafless while white root runners circle tightly around the pot edges and growth stalls?
solve_it_like_this: Unpot the entire mint clump every 4 to 6 months; Pudina grows aggressively and exhausts shallow pot space quickly.
Divide the root clump with clean garden shears into 3 or 4 smaller portions, keeping young fresh root runners.
Replant the healthiest runners into fresh compost-rich soil mix and water well; lush new green leaves will emerge within 7–10 days.

common_problems.problem: Powdery mildew and mint rust during humid weather
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Do you see a white powdery dusting on leaf surfaces or rusty orange-brown spots underneath leaves during humid monsoon periods?
solve_it_like_this: Immediately snip off and discard severely infected stems in the trash bin (do not put in compost).
Space pots apart to promote good airflow and keep the plant in a breezy, sun-drenched spot.
Spray with an organic baking soda remedy (1 tsp baking soda + 1/2 tsp mild liquid soap in 1 litre of water) in the morning.
Water strictly into the soil at root level; keep foliage dry during cloudy monsoon days.

watering_every_days.note: Peppermint relishes consistently moist, cool potting soil. In scorching summer temperatures (>35°C), water every morning, making sure moisture reaches the entire root zone. Do not allow the root zone to dry to bone, or stems will collapse. During the monsoon, maintain free drainage holes to avoid waterlogged stagnation.

soil.in_simple_words: Rich, moisture-retentive, humus-packed potting loam with excellent aeration and good drainage.
soil.mix_recipe: 2 parts garden loam + 2 parts aged vermicompost + 1 part coco peat + 1 part coarse sand or perlite + 2 tbsp neem cake powder

pet_and_child_safety.note: Safe and edible for culinary and herbal tea use. Safe around children and pets in fresh garden leaf form; keep concentrated peppermint essential oil away from cats and dogs, as pure menthol is irritating to pet respiratory and digestive systems.

common_problems.problem: Extreme dry heat stress and drooping foliage
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are leaves curling inward, losing their dark green gloss, and wilting limp during hot North/Central Indian dry summer afternoons?
solve_it_like_this: Shift the container to morning sun only (or under 50% green garden shade netting).
Place the pot on a saucer filled with moist river pebbles to generate localized evaporative humidity without drowning roots.
Mulch the topsoil with dried leaves or coco peat to preserve root coolness.

common_problems.problem: Mint rust (Puccinia menthae fungal infection)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Do you see bright orange-brown or dark pustules erupting on the underside of peppermint leaves with yellow patches on top?
solve_it_like_this: Snip off diseased stems at the base immediately and throw them away in household waste.
Ensure pots are spaced out in a breezy area with good morning sunlight.
Spray the plant with an organic cold-pressed neem oil solution (5 ml/L + 2 ml mild soap) every 5 days.
Water strictly at ground level; avoid overhead sprinkling.

common_problems.problem: Leaf-roller caterpillars chewing foliage
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are top peppermint leaves spun together with fine white silk webbing, with chewed holes and tiny black droppings inside?
solve_it_like_this: Gently unroll folded leaf clusters by hand and pick off small green caterpillars.
Spray an organic bio-pesticide containing Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) or an organic crushed garlic-chilli extract in the evening.
Regularly trim and harvest upper sprigs to deny caterpillars nesting sites.

common_problems.problem: Fungal stem rot and damp leaf decay in heavy rains
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are lower stems near the soil surface turning black, soft, and mushy during persistent monsoon wet spells?
solve_it_like_this: Elevate the pot on brick stands so bottom drainage holes drain freely without pooling on wet balcony floors.
Thin crowded growth to allow wind to circulate through the base of the plant.
Dust the topsoil with dry wood ash or ground cinnamon powder to suppress soil fungus.

local_names.hindi: स्वीट तुलसी / मीठी तुलसी / इटैलियन बेसिल

watering_every_days.note: Sweet Basil has broad, lush leaves with a high rate of water loss in dry weather. Water thoroughly when the top inch of soil feels dry. In hot summer months, water early every morning. Never wet the foliage late in the evening to prevent fungal leaf spots. In winter, reduce watering as growth slows down and protect from cold drafts.

soil.in_simple_words: Rich, loose, well-draining garden soil packed with organic compost to support rapid, lush leaf growth.
soil.mix_recipe: 2 parts fertile garden loam + 2 parts vermicompost or leaf mold + 1 part coco peat + 1 part coarse sand or perlite + 2 tbsp neem cake powder

pet_and_child_safety.note: Completely non-toxic to humans, children, dogs, and cats according to the ASPCA. Fully culinary-safe for fresh pesto, pastas, and salads.

common_problems.problem: Flowering (bolting) leading to tough, bitter leaves
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are tall flower spikes blooming at the stem tips, causing the leaves below to become smaller, sparse, tough, and bitter?
solve_it_like_this: Pinch off all terminal flower buds as soon as they appear to redirect energy back into lush leaf production.
Prune the top one-third of stems every 2 to 3 weeks just above a leaf node; this stimulates dual bushy side branches.
Harvest outer leaves and sprigs regularly for cooking; frequent harvesting prevents the plant from setting seed.

common_problems.problem: Basil downy mildew and leaf yellowing
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are leaves developing pale yellowish patches between veins, followed by purplish-gray downy spores under the leaf surfaces?
solve_it_like_this: Water strictly at the base of the stems in early morning; keep leaves dry at all times.
Ensure wide spacing between pots on the balcony for maximum air circulation and morning sun exposure.
Remove and discard severely affected leaves; spray remaining foliage with a mild bio-fungicide like Trichoderma viride or dilute baking soda spray (1 tsp/L).

common_problems.problem: Aphids and whiteflies sucking sap from tender leaves
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are clusters of tiny green insects under leaves or tiny white flies fluttering around when stems are touched, leaving sticky residue?
solve_it_like_this: Hang yellow sticky glue cards 15 cm above the foliage to trap flying whiteflies and winged aphids.
Spray an organic emulsion of 5 ml cold-pressed neem oil + 2 ml mild liquid soap per litre of water under the leaves in late evening.
Rinse culinary leaves with clean drinking water before preparing food.

common_problems.problem: Winter cold shock and blackened leaves
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are leaves turning translucent black, limp, and dropping off when night temperatures drop below 12°C during North Indian winters?
solve_it_like_this: Move the pot indoors to a sunny south-facing windowsill or sheltered warm balcony away from cold night breezes.
Cut back watering significantly during cold spells; wet roots in cold soil rot rapidly.
Take softwood stem cuttings in October to root in water indoors as backups for the following spring.

watering_every_days.note: Lemongrass is a fast-growing, heavy-drinking tropical clumping grass during warm weather. In hot Indian summers, soak the pot thoroughly every morning; if blade tips curl inward and turn straw-like, increase watering. It relishes heavy monsoon rains provided bottom drainage holes are free. Reduce watering in winter when vegetative growth slows.

soil.in_simple_words: Rich, loamy, highly fertile soil in a broad, deep container (at least 12–14 inches wide) that gives its expanding rhizomes plenty of room.
soil.mix_recipe: 2 parts garden loam + 2 parts well-rotted cow dung manure (gobar khaad) or vermicompost + 1 part coarse river sand + 1 part coco peat + 1 cup neem cake powder

pet_and_child_safety.note: Completely non-toxic and culinary-safe for humans; widely used in Indian chai and herbal decoctions. Safe around pets in typical garden situations, though cats or dogs should be discouraged from chewing large fibrous quantities as rough grass blades can induce mechanical stomach upset.

common_problems.problem: Leaf blight and rust streaks during monsoon
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are long grass blades displaying reddish-brown streaks, dry necrotic tips, or dusty orange spots during warm, humid rainy spells?
solve_it_like_this: Cut back affected outer blades to 2 inches from the base with clean shears and discard clippings.
Ensure the pot sits in full open sunshine and breezy conditions to dry wet foliage rapidly.
Spray the remaining clump with an organic cold-pressed neem oil emulsion (5 ml neem oil + 2 ml mild soap per litre of water).

common_problems.problem: Rootbound clump congestion and center hollow dieback
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Is the center of the grass clump turning brown, woody, and hollow while outer stalks push hard against the pot rim?
solve_it_like_this: Unpot the entire root mass in late winter or early monsoon (February or July).
Divide the thick clump into 3–4 smaller sections using a sharp serrated knife, ensuring each division has healthy roots and 3–5 sturdy stalks.
Cut back top blades by 50% to minimize transplant shock and replant divisions into fresh manure-rich potting soil.

common_problems.problem: Red spider mites during hot dry summer
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Do you see pale stippled yellowish leaf blades with dusty fine webbing around leaf sheaths in dry 40°C weather?
solve_it_like_this: Hose down the entire grass clump thoroughly with a forceful jet of water to wash away mite colonies and webs.
Keep soil consistently moist and avoid positioning against hot, reflective concrete walls.
Apply an evening spray of organic neem oil emulsion (5 ml/L) once a week.

common_problems.problem: Pale yellowing blades (Nitrogen deficiency)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are grass blades turning uniform pale yellow-green with thin, slow-growing stalks despite regular watering?
solve_it_like_this: Top-dress the pot with 2–3 large handfuls of aged vermicompost or well-composted cow dung manure every month.
Drench the root zone with organic liquid seaweed extract or fermented compost tea every 15 days.
Ensure container drainage is free so vital nutrients are not washed out by stagnant water.

watering_every_days.note: Rosemary is native to arid Mediterranean rocky slopes and cannot tolerate wet, boggy potting soil. Water deeply only when the top 2 inches of soil feel completely dry. In the Indian monsoon, keep the pot sheltered under a balcony roof; continuous rain on waterlogged roots is the #1 killer of rosemary in India. In winter, water sparingly every 7 to 10 days.

soil.in_simple_words: Super gritty, rock-filled, ultra-porous potting mix that lets water flush straight through and never holds standing moisture; prefers porous terracotta pots and neutral-to-alkaline pH.
soil.mix_recipe: 2 parts coarse river sand or crushed cinder + 2 parts pumice or fine gravel + 1 part garden soil + 1 part vermicompost + 1 tbsp crushed limestone or eggshell powder + 1 tbsp neem cake powder

pet_and_child_safety.note: Completely non-toxic to humans, children, dogs, and cats according to the ASPCA. Widely grown as a safe culinary herb and natural aromatic repellent.

common_problems.problem: Monsoon root rot and stem collar rot (Phytophthora fungus)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are needle-like leaves turning dull brown or black from the base upwards, drooping limply with soft mushy stems near the soil line?
solve_it_like_this: Immediately move the pot out of open rain into an airy, covered balcony space.
Check drainage holes; if the soil is soggy, gently slide the plant out, trim away mushy black roots, and dust with cinnamon powder or organic Trichoderma bio-fungicide.
Repot into a high-grit mix containing at least 50% cinder, gravel, or coarse sand in an unglazed terracotta pot.
Withhold watering until the soil is bone dry; never allow pots to sit in water collection saucers.

common_problems.problem: Powdery mildew coating needles in stagnant air
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Do you see a dull grayish-white powder coating needle clusters during humid monsoon or cloudy autumn weeks?
solve_it_like_this: Move the pot to your balcony's sunniest and breeziest location; stagnant humid air triggers fungal outbreaks.
Prune congested inner branches to open up airflow through the core of the bush.
Spray an organic solution of 1 tsp baking soda + 1/2 tsp mild liquid soap in 1 litre of water in early morning sun.

common_problems.problem: Spider mites and spittlebugs on tender shoots
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are needles turning speckled yellow with fine cobwebs, or do you notice foamy white froth ('cuckoo spit') nestled in branch joints?
solve_it_like_this: Wipe off foamy spittlebug nests with a wet cotton rag or wash off with a sharp water jet.
Spray an organic neem oil solution (5 ml cold-pressed neem oil + 2 ml mild dish soap per litre of water) once a week in late afternoon.
Avoid using chemical pesticides that kill natural beneficial predators.

common_problems.problem: Leggy, sparse growth and premature lower stem woodiness
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are lower branches bare, thick, and brown with green foliage only at the distant tips, looking sparse and spindly?
solve_it_like_this: Ensure the plant receives at least 6 to 8 hours of direct unfiltered sunlight daily to prevent stretching.
Prune the top 2 to 3 inches of green sprigs regularly for kitchen use; frequent tip-pruning forces bushy side branching.
Never cut deep into old, bare brown wood that lacks needles, as rosemary rarely generates new buds from old woody stems.

watering_every_days.note: Thyme despises waterlogged roots and thrives on dry, lean conditions. Allow the potting soil to dry out almost completely between waterings. In hot Indian summers, water in the early morning when the pot feels light. During the monsoon, shelter pots under rain covers as standing water around its fine root system will cause fatal fungal rot within 48 hours.

soil.in_simple_words: Lean, fast-draining, gritty sandy soil with minimal organic matter retention; thrives best in porous terracotta containers.
soil.mix_recipe: 2 parts coarse sand or fine gravel + 2 parts cinder or perlite + 1 part garden soil + 1 part aged vermicompost + 1 tbsp crushed limestone or eggshell powder

pet_and_child_safety.note: Non-toxic to humans, children, dogs, and cats according to the ASPCA. Safe for culinary use and pet-friendly in household herb gardens.

common_problems.problem: Monsoon fungal dieback and root rot (Rhizoctonia/damping off)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are entire stems turning black, limp, and rotting into a mushy clump during rainy or humid monsoon weeks?
solve_it_like_this: Immediately shift the pot away from rainfall to a dry, well-ventilated balcony under full breeze.
Snip away all blackened, mushy stems right to the base with sterilized scissors.
Top-dress the soil surface with 1 cm of coarse pea gravel or cinder grit to keep the lower stems from touching damp soil.
Withhold watering until the soil is completely dry, and drench the base with an organic bio-fungicide like Trichoderma viride.

common_problems.problem: Two-spotted spider mites in hot dry weather
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are tiny thyme leaves turning speckled yellow, looking dusty and webbed in dry April–May weather?
solve_it_like_this: Spray the plant underside with a fine mist of cold water early in the morning to increase humidity.
Apply an organic spray of 5 ml cold-pressed neem oil and 2 ml liquid castile soap per litre of water once a week in the evening.
Ensure the plant is not kept near hot reflective concrete walls that trap dry radiating heat.

common_problems.problem: Woody center dieback and lack of pruning
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Is the center of the thyme bush turning brown, woody, and barren while leafy growth only occurs at the outer sprawling tips?
solve_it_like_this: Lightly shear back the outer top green growth by one-third in spring (February–March) to encourage fresh shoots from the center.
Never cut back into old, bare brown woody stems, as thyme cannot generate new buds from old wood.
Propagate fresh vigorous replacement plants every 2 years by stem cuttings or layering trailing branches.

watering_every_days.note: Oregano is a drought-tolerant Mediterranean herb that prefers lean, dry conditions. Overwatering is the single most common cause of failure in Indian gardens. Water deeply when the top 1 to 2 inches of soil feel completely dry, letting excess water drain out immediately. In monsoon, keep the pot in an airy covered balcony away from continuous lashing rains.

soil.in_simple_words: Gritty, sharply draining, light sandy-loam potting mix with modest organic content and slightly alkaline pH.
soil.mix_recipe: 2 parts river sand or crushed cinder + 2 parts garden soil + 1 part vermicompost + 1 part perlite + 1 tbsp horticultural lime or crushed eggshell powder

pet_and_child_safety.note: Completely safe and non-toxic for culinary human consumption. Fresh oregano in small culinary garnishes is safe for household pets, though pets should not consume large amounts of leaves or concentrated oregano essential oil due to strong aromatic phenols.

common_problems.problem: Monsoon root rot and fungal collar rot
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are leaves turning yellow, limp, and dark brown at the base with blackened, rotting roots during prolonged monsoon showers?
solve_it_like_this: Move the pot immediately to a sheltered, rain-protected balcony with active breeze.
Check drainage holes to ensure no water is trapped; empty saucers beneath the pot immediately.
Prune away rotting stems and top-dress the soil surface with coarse gravel or cinder to prevent wet soil from resting against lower leaves.
Drench soil with organic bio-fungicide (Trichoderma viride or Pseudomonas fluorescens) if rot symptoms appear.

common_problems.problem: Aphids and spider mites on tender growth
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Do you see tiny green bugs on new shoot tips or fine stippling and webbing on the underside of oregano leaves?
solve_it_like_this: Wash off pest colonies with a sharp morning water spray.
Spray an organic mixture of 5 ml neem oil + 2 ml mild dish soap per litre of water onto foliage in late evening.
Prune heavily infested sprigs and wash kitchen herbs before consumption.

common_problems.problem: Loss of essential oil potency and weak flavor
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are leaves growing large, dark green, and watery but lacking the characteristic punchy oregano fragrance and taste?
solve_it_like_this: Stop adding heavy nitrogen fertilizers; rich soils dilute oregano's essential oils.
Increase direct sun exposure to at least 6 full hours daily; sun intensity concentrates aromatic volatile oils.
Allow the soil to dry out more between waterings to simulate its native semi-arid Mediterranean habitat.

watering_every_days.note: Coriander is a cool-season annual with delicate, shallow taproots. In Indian winters (October–February), water gently whenever the top half-inch of soil dries. In hot dry summer months (March–June), coriander struggles and bolts to seed rapidly; keep the potting mix consistently damp and provide cool afternoon shade. Always water with a gentle rose-head can to avoid flattening tender seedlings.

soil.in_simple_words: Light, friable, fertile, compost-rich sandy loam that drains freely while retaining steady moisture.
soil.mix_recipe: 2 parts garden loam + 2 parts vermicompost or leaf compost + 1 part coarse sand + 1 part coco peat + 2 tbsp neem cake powder

pet_and_child_safety.note: Completely safe and non-toxic for humans, children, dogs, and cats. Widely consumed raw in daily culinary dishes.

common_problems.problem: Premature bolting and flowering in summer heat
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are stems suddenly shooting up tall and spindly, with feathery fern-like leaves and tiny white flower umbels instead of broad leafy greens?
solve_it_like_this: Understand that temperatures above 30°C and long day-lengths trigger natural bolting to set coriander seed.
Grow coriander in bright partial shade or morning-sun-only locations during March to June, avoiding hot afternoon glare.
Sow heat-tolerant/slow-bolt cultivars, mulch the soil surface to keep roots cool, and practice succession sowing every 2 weeks.
Harvest outer stems frequently using the 'cut-and-come-again' method before central flower stalks elongate.

common_problems.problem: Damping off in young seedlings (Pythium/Rhizoctonia fungal wilt)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are tender young coriander sprouts collapsing at the soil line, looking water-soaked, shriveled, and dying in patches?
solve_it_like_this: Avoid overcrowding seeds; crush whole coriander seeds into halves (split seeds) and sow them spaced 1 to 2 inches apart.
Ensure pots have multiple unobstructed drainage holes and use a light, sterilized, free-draining seed-starting mix.
Water using a fine misting spray in early morning; never overwater or leave the soil waterlogged.
Treat seeds with Trichoderma viride bio-fungicide powder before sowing.

common_problems.problem: Powdery mildew (White powdery coating on foliage)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are leaves and stems coated with a dusty white flour-like fungal growth during warm dry winter afternoons following cool humid nights?
solve_it_like_this: Thin the crop to allow sunlight and breeze to reach the base of each plant.
Spray foliage with an organic solution of 1 teaspoon baking soda + 2 drops mild soap in 1 litre of water at the first sign of white spots.
Avoid splashing water on the foliage late in the evening; water only the soil surface in the morning.

common_problems.problem: Green peach aphids and coriander aphids
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are clusters of tiny green or yellowish insects crowding the tender inner leaf shoots, causing curling and stunted yellow leaves?
solve_it_like_this: Wash them off gently with a handheld spray bottle of cool water.
Spray an organic solution of 3 to 5 ml cold-pressed neem oil + 1 ml mild dish soap per litre of water in late afternoon.
Dust fine wood ash or diatomaceous earth around the base to deter crawling pests.

watering_every_days.note: Parsley has a long, delicate taproot that requires consistently moist, evenly damp soil. Never let the root ball completely dry out, as drought stress causes tough, yellowing, bitter leaves. In Indian summers, water early in the morning and provide afternoon shade. In winter and monsoons, water when the top inch dries, ensuring water flushes through freely without waterlogging.

soil.in_simple_words: Deep, rich, moisture-retentive yet well-drained loamy soil with plenty of organic matter in a pot at least 10–12 inches deep to accommodate its long taproot.
soil.mix_recipe: 2 parts garden loam + 2 parts aged vermicompost or composted cow manure + 1 part coco peat + 1 part coarse sand or perlite + 2 tbsp neem cake powder

pet_and_child_safety.note: Completely safe and edible for humans and children. Curly/flat parsley in small dietary quantities is safe for dogs and commonly used as a natural breath freshener; however, avoid letting pets gorge on massive quantities, and do not confuse with toxic wild carrot or spring parsley (Cymopterus watsonii).

common_problems.problem: Summer heat stress and lower leaf yellowing
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are outer leaf stems turning bright yellow, wilting limp, and drying up under hot summer temperatures exceeding 32°C?
solve_it_like_this: Move the pot to a bright morning-sun location that is fully shaded from harsh midday and afternoon heat.
Ensure the deep potting mix remains consistently damp; mulch the top with coco peat or rice husk to keep taproots cool.
Harvest outer stems regularly to relieve transpiration load on the root system.

common_problems.problem: Septoria leaf spot (Fungal brown spots with yellow halos)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Do you see small sunken brown circular spots with yellow halos on leaf blades during warm humid periods?
solve_it_like_this: Prune away and safely dispose of all spotted leaves to prevent fungal spores from spreading.
Water strictly at the soil base using a watering can with a narrow spout; never wet parsley leaves directly.
Spray remaining foliage with an organic copper-free bio-fungicide like Trichoderma viride or dilute baking soda spray (1 tsp/L).

common_problems.problem: Extremely slow germination (Parsley seeds taking 3–4 weeks to sprout)
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Have you sown parsley seeds but see zero sprouts emerging even after 2 to 3 weeks?
solve_it_like_this: Understand that parsley seed coats contain natural germination inhibitors (furanocoumarins) that make sprouting naturally sluggish.
Soak parsley seeds in warm water (approx 40°C) overnight for 12 to 24 hours before sowing to leach out inhibitors.
Keep the seedbed constantly damp by covering the pot loosely with a moist burlap cloth or paper towel until sprouts appear.

common_problems.problem: Caterpillars / leaf chewers
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are entire leaf stems being stripped bare overnight with large green-and-black striped caterpillars feeding on foliage?
solve_it_like_this: Hand-pick caterpillars off the plants and relocate them (many are beneficial swallowtail butterfly larvae).
If damage is excessive, spray with organic Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) or an organic neem oil spray in late evening.
Cover young parsley plants with fine horticultural insect netting if moth pressure is intense.
